subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the orthocentre of the triangle whose sides are 7x+y−10=0, x−2y+5=0, x+y+2=0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.16 — LAQ chapter 1 The Straight Line, answer 3. No appearance years are printed against this answer. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this LAQ chapter. It is not a bare guess: the book prints its own numbered 'Step-1 / Step-2 / Step-3' structure against this very answer, and the split follows those printed steps, giving the two long eliminations two marks each and the closing solve two, with one for setting up. The only printed splits in this UNIT are on SAQ answer 59 (book p.63, 1+1+2) and VSAQ answer 98 (p.83, 1+1) — both shorter cuts, so neither fixes a 7-mark shape. Paper position: Maths-1B Section C runs Q18-Q24 at 7 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. The book prints its own boxed 'SOLUTION STEPS' panel beside this answer, in three stages — I. solve two lines to get vertex A, then the altitude through it; II. solve another pair to get B, then the altitude through it; III. solve the two altitudes to get O. The split follows those three printed stages, with one mark for the first vertex. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82).
